newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Denmark strike forces Lufthansa rejig.
newsitem.headline: Denmark strike forces Lufthansa rejig.

text.p: A three-day old truckers' strike in Denmark has forced German carrier Deutsche Lufthansa AG's cargo division to replace some trucking services with a larger freight carrier.

Jorgen Jorgensen, cargo manager Denmark for the airline's autonomous freight unit Lufthansa Cargo, said an Airbus 310 with a capacity of about 10 tonnes was flying its daily Copenhagen-Frankfurt flights instead of the usual Airbus 320.
He said the change had been made for the first time on Tuesday. It was too early to tell how much the strike would cost the airline.
"We have lost some shipments due to the size. We can only load shipments onto the trucks which are up to 160 cm tall compared to three metres," Jorgensen told Reuters.
The Airbus 310 had about eight more tonnes capacity than the Airbus 320, he said.
"For the time being feeder services are stopped until further notice," Jorgensen said, adding that the airline normally had daily trucking services from Frankfurt to Copenhagen and Billund and back.
Danish truckers are striking to protest government plans to cut drivers' overseas subsistence allowances, sealing off a land border with Germany and blocking most seaports.
